project.name: davinci-license-plate-detector
project.one_liner: DaVinci Resolve plugin that detects, tracks, and destructively anonymises vehicle license plates (Swiss plates prioritised), with the resulting matte exposed as a mask for downstream effects.

pros: OFX Interact API gives viewer overlay + click capture
cons: Resolve ships partial OFX Interact support; overlay handles must be verified per page
no native multi-output mask port; mask must go out via alpha channel or a separate 'mask-only' render mode

candidate_integration_surfaces.surface: Fusion native plugin (Fusion SDK, C++) or Fuse (Lua)
cons: Fuse cannot host a neural network; needs a C++ Fusion plugin or an out-of-process inference server

candidate_integration_surfaces.surface: Resolve Scripting API (Python/Lua) + Workflow Integration panel
pros: can drive inference out-of-process and write Fusion comps / power windows
cons: no per-frame pixel access; cannot draw in viewer; unsuitable as the primary renderer

host.recommended_architecture: OFX plugin with Interact overlay for click-to-seed and quad handles; inference in an out-of-process engine (ONNX Runtime / CoreML / TensorRT) over shared memory; track stored as keyframed OFX params (4 corner points per plate instance); mask emitted on the alpha channel with a 'Mask Only' output mode so it can feed Resolve alpha/External Matte and Fusion MatteControl.

epistemologies._definition: The distinct ways the system comes to 'know' where a plate is. Each has its own evidence source, uncertainty model, and failure mode.

items.name: Empirical / learned prior (detection)
items.mode_of_knowing: Inductive inference from a supervised dataset via a convolutional or transformer detector.
items.representation: Oriented bounding box (OBB) or 4-point quadrilateral via corner keypoint regression; class probability; confidence score.
items.uncertainty: Per-detection confidence; calibrated via temperature scaling on a held-out Swiss set.
failure_modes: false positives on signage / bumper stickers
misses under motion blur or specular glare

items.name: Human-in-the-loop ground truth (click seeding)
items.mode_of_knowing: Testimonial: the operator asserts 'a plate is here' by clicking in the viewer.
items.evidence: Seed point (x, y) on the seed frame, in normalised canonical coordinates.
items.representation: Seed acts as a spatial prior / prompt that gates detection to the neighbourhood of the click and disambiguates multiple candidate plates.
items.uncertainty: Treated as near-certain for existence; imprecise for extent (click may land off-centre or on an occluder).
failure_modes: click on reflection of a plate
click on a plate that is already partially out of frame

items.name: Bayesian state estimation (tracking)
items.mode_of_knowing: Recursive predict-observe-correct over time using a motion model and per-frame observations.
items.evidence: Sequence of detections / optical-flow measurements / planar homography estimates.
items.representation: State vector per plate: 4 corners (or centre, size, rotation, perspective) + velocities; covariance matrix.
items.uncertainty: Covariance grows during prediction-only (occluded / out-of-frame) frames; shrinks on confirmed observations.
failure_modes: ID switch between two adjacent plates

items.name: Appearance identity (re-identification)
items.mode_of_knowing: Similarity: the object reappearing is the same object because its embedding matches.
items.evidence: Crop of the plate region fed to an embedding network; optionally OCR string of the plate.
items.representation: Feature vector; cosine similarity; optional plate string with per-character confidence.
items.uncertainty: Similarity threshold; ambiguous when plates are small or blurred.

items.name: Visibility state reasoning (occlusion logic)
items.mode_of_knowing: Abductive: the best explanation for a missing observation is chosen from a finite set of hypotheses.
items.evidence: Detection presence/absence, predicted position vs frame bounds, partial-overlap ratio, optical-flow consistency.
items.representation: Finite-state machine per track: TENTATIVE → CONFIRMED → PARTIALLY_OCCLUDED → FULLY_OCCLUDED → OUT_OF_FRAME → REACQUIRED → TERMINATED.
items.uncertainty: Explicit per-state confidence decay; operator can override any state on any frame.
failure_modes: declaring TERMINATED before a legitimate return

items.name: Operator verification (falsification gate)
items.mode_of_knowing: Critical rationalism: a detection/track is accepted only after the operator has had the chance to falsify it.
items.evidence: Viewer overlay of the quad and mask; scrub through the tracked range.
items.representation: Explicit 'Detect' then 'Track' buttons; nothing is committed to render until the operator has seen the detection on the seed frame.
items.uncertainty: Human error; mitigated by making every keyframe editable after tracking.
failure_modes: operator approves a quad that is too tight
operator forgets to re-verify after retiming

items.name: Information-theoretic irreversibility (anonymisation guarantee)
items.mode_of_knowing: Deductive: the output cannot be inverted because the information required to invert it has been destroyed, not hidden.
items.evidence: Analysis of the obfuscation operator's channel capacity and its resistance to known attacks.
items.representation: Obfuscation = lossy quantisation ∘ stochastic permutation ∘ temporal jitter; the random seed is discarded after use and never written to metadata.
items.uncertainty: Zero by construction for the destroyed bits; residual risk only in untouched pixels outside the mask.
failure_modes: insufficient block size leaves legible characters
deterministic seed reused across frames enables temporal averaging

axioms._definition: Invariants that must hold for every build. If any is violated the plugin is considered broken regardless of other features.

items.name: Destructiveness
items.statement: Any anonymising output mode (blur, pixelize, randomize) must be non-invertible from the rendered frames alone. No seed, key, or side-channel that permits reconstruction is ever persisted.

items.name: Source non-destruction
items.statement: The plugin never modifies the source media; all effects live in the timeline/node graph and are removable.

items.name: Temporal coherence
items.statement: Across consecutive frames the mask must vary smoothly in position, scale, and shape; state transitions (occluded, out-of-frame, return) must not cause a single-frame pop.

items.name: Fail-safe coverage
items.statement: When uncertain, over-cover rather than under-cover: the mask expands with predicted covariance during occlusion; a plate is never un-masked because tracking is unsure.

items.name: Swiss-first priors
items.statement: Detector, aspect-ratio priors, and test corpus are weighted for Swiss plate formats first; other formats are supported but never at the expense of Swiss recall.

items.name: Multi-instance independence
items.statement: Each plate is an independent track with its own lifecycle, keyframes, and parameters; adding or deleting one never alters another.

items.name: Operator sovereignty
items.statement: Every automated result (quad, keyframe, visibility state) is editable by the operator, and manual edits are never overwritten by a re-run unless explicitly requested.

items.name: Two-stage commit
items.statement: Detection and tracking are separate user actions ('Detect license plate' then 'Track license plate'); tracking is never triggered implicitly.

items.name: Mask exportability
items.statement: The matte is available as a standalone signal (alpha channel / mask output / Mask Only mode) so it can drive arbitrary downstream effects, not only the built-in obfuscators.

items.name: Determinism of non-random paths
items.statement: Given the same keyframes and parameters, all non-stochastic outputs (mask shape, blur) are bit-identical between preview and final render; only the deliberately random obfuscators are frame-unique.

items.name: Colour-space neutrality
items.statement: Mask generation operates on a linearised luma/working-space copy; obfuscation is applied in the host's working colour space so results are consistent across Rec.709, DaVinci Wide Gamut, and ACES timelines.

fractals._definition: Self-similar structures that recur at multiple scales of the system. Recognising them lets the same code path and the same mental model serve every level.

items.name: Predict → Observe → Correct loop
items.pattern: The Kalman cycle repeats at every temporal scale.

scales.instance: predict corner positions, observe detection/flow, correct state
predict trajectory across the gap, observe re-appearance, correct the interpolated keyframes bidirectionally
predict that a plate persists, observe a cut, terminate / re-seed
operator predicts a track is fine, observes a slip on scrub, corrects a keyframe

items.name: Seed → Detect → Verify → Track lifecycle
items.pattern: The four-step user workflow is identical for one plate, for N plates, and for re-seeding after a return-to-frame.

scales.instance: click, detect, verify, track
the same lifecycle instantiated per track, run independently (A6)
when re-ID fails, the operator re-seeds mid-clip and the sub-track is stitched into the parent tracklet

items.name: Coarse-to-fine pyramid
items.pattern: Detection and tracking both refine a coarse hypothesis to a fine one.

scales.instance: Lucas-Kanade / detector runs on downsampled levels first
axis-aligned bbox → oriented bbox → 4-point quad → sub-pixel corner refinement
hard quad → expanded/contracted morphology → feathered soft edge

items.name: Containment hierarchy
items.pattern: Every level contains the next as an independent unit with the same interface (id, bounds, confidence, state).

scales.instance: clips
plate tracks
keyframes
4 corners + visibility state
characters (only for OCR-assisted re-ID; never persisted)

items.name: Mask operator composition
items.pattern: Every output modifier is a pure function mask → mask or (image, mask) → image, so they compose in any order and the whole chain is itself one such function.

scales.instance: expand, contract, feather
blur, pixelize, randomize
the ordered stack is one composite operator applied per plate then unioned

items.name: Uncertainty inflation
items.pattern: Whatever the level, lack of evidence expands the region rather than shrinking it (A4).

scales.instance: feather widens with track covariance
predicted quad grows by covariance-derived margin during occlusion
coast window extends the mask past the last confirmed frame by a user-set 'hold' count

factors._definition: Independent variables that change how the system behaves or how well it performs. Grouped by the layer they act on.

swiss_formats.notes: canton code + up to 6 digits, black on white, no shields
Swiss cross left, canton coat of arms right
some cantons issue the short variant on the rear
canton code on the first line, number on the second
yellow ground, black text; hard case

swiss_formats.type: dealer / temporary (U, Z, CD, CC, AT)
swiss_formats.notes: special suffix letters; temporary plates have a red stripe

secondary_formats: DE / AT / FR / IT (blue band + national letters)

occluders: the car's own body during turns (self-occlusion)
frame_events: cuts inside a clip (multicam / speed ramps)
optical: resolution (plate height in pixels: <12 px is the practical floor for detection)

seed_gating_radius_px.note: search radius around the click, scaled with clip resolution

aspect_ratio_prior_weight.note: penalises candidates far from Swiss ratios (A5)

inference_resolution.note: letterboxed; higher improves small-plate recall at a speed cost

max_age_frames.note: frames a track may coast fully unobserved before TERMINATED; operator can extend

partial_occlusion_ratio.note: visible fraction below which state → PARTIALLY_OCCLUDED and mask holds last full shape

expand_contract_px.op: morphological dilation (positive) / erosion (negative) on the quad matte

feather_px.op: Gaussian falloff on the matte edge; interacts with A4 (feather never reveals the plate core)

blur.irreversibility_note: Gaussian blur alone is partially invertible (deconvolution); when 'destructive' is on, blur is followed by quantisation + noise

pixelize.irreversibility_note: static mosaic is vulnerable to temporal-averaging attacks; destructive mode jitters block phase per frame and randomises within-block colour

randomize_pixels.seed_policy: fresh CSPRNG seed per frame per plate, discarded after render (A1)

destructive_lock.note: when true the obfuscator chain is forced through quantise+permute so that no parameter combination yields an invertible result; UI shows a lock badge

mask_only_output.note: outputs the matte as white-on-black RGB and in alpha; disables obfuscators; satisfies A9

per_instance_override.note: each plate track can override any modifier; defaults inherit from the clip-level settings (A6)

state_indicators: confirmed / occluded / out-of-frame colour coding on the overlay
keyframe markers on the timeline ruler
feedback: progress bar with cancel during track
warning when destructive lock is off

host_and_platform.realtime_target: ≥ 24 fps at 1080p for mask + blur once tracked; detection may be offline
host_and_platform.ofx_api: 1.4 with Interact suite; verify overlay behaviour on Edit vs Color vs Fusion pages
host_and_platform.cache_interaction: track data is stored in plugin params so Resolve's render cache invalidates correctly on edit

training_corpus: synthetic Swiss plates composited onto vehicles (domain randomisation)
public plate datasets re-weighted (CCPD, UFPR-ALPR, OpenALPR benchmark) as secondary

anonymisation: OCR success rate on output (must be ~0)
super-resolution attack success over 100-frame stacks (must be ~0)

data_and_evaluation.privacy_and_legal_context: Swiss plates are personal data under the nDSG / FADP; the destructive requirement (A1) exists so that rendered deliverables carry no recoverable plate information.

user_stories_to_components.story: click on the license plate in the viewer
when it's good, click 'track license plate'
randomize pixels, blur, pixelize with reversal protection
use it as a mask for other effects
